question: Which of the following enzymes can be considered a good marker of drug-induced hemolytic anemia ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Drug-induced hemolytic anemia" -> "red blood cell destruction" -> "increased lactate dehydrogenase" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Drug-induced hemolytic anemia" -> "red blood cell destruction" -> "increased aspartate aminotransferase" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Drug-induced hemolytic anemia" -> "red blood cell destruction" -> "increased creatine kinase" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Drug-induced hemolytic anemia" -> "red blood cell destruction" -> "decreased glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase" -> 60%
analysis: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is a good marker for hemolytic anemia, including drug-induced hemolytic anemia. This is because LDH is released from red blood cells when they are destroyed, leading to elevated levels in the blood. While Glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PDH) deficiency can predispose individuals to hemolytic anemia, it is not a marker of the condition itself.
